messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: increased OOM rate on inference-pool-3 (kv-cache service). 5xx spike starting at 1768004300. Pager: @sara oncall.

sara: seeing lots of 13xx/GPU OOMs in the malloc logs and high fragmented cache sizes. Routing to infra. tagging #incidents.

miguel: I'm on it. quick q — is this affecting hosted customers or only Dedicated nodes? any customer-facing 5xxs?

anya: datapoints: CloudWatch shows CUDA_OOM errors at 1768004280, 1768004312. Error rate -> 4x normal; tail latency also up. SLO alert firing.

sara: initial impact: some customer requests returning 503/502, throughput dropped ~30% on pool-3. A few dedicated customers reported degraded completions.

devops: logs from node-7 show repeated `cudaMemoryGetInfo` fragmentation, arena fragmentation pattern. Sample from node-7:
E Cuda: Cuda runtime error: out of memory (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation)
stack: /opt/runtime/inference::allocate_kv_cache+0x1b2
cache_arena: used=12.7G committed=32G arenas=18

nora: that 'arenas=18' looks like caching allocator created many arenas -> fragmentation. Could be triggered by long sequences + continuous batching.

miguel: hypothesis: continuous batching + a sudden set of long context requests caused many large allocations that fragmented GPU caches. CUDA caching allocator didn't release large blocks fast enough -> subsequent allocations OOM. Also saw `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` unset on these containers.

rahul: can we short-circuit KV cache growth? options: 1) disable continuous batching on pool-3 2) force GC and clear per-request KV cache after completion 3) reduce max_batch_tokens / cap sequence length. Which is fastest?

sara: priority is reduce customer 5xxs now. Miguel, can you flip batching off for the pool? we have a rollout knob `batching.continuous.enabled` per pool.

miguel: performing: `rbacctl set-config --pool inference-pool-3 --key batching.continuous.enabled=false --actor miguel` applying now. will monitor.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: config change recorded (miguel) - rolling to nodes in pool-3 (6 nodes) - change id cfg_1768004321_1

anya: after toggle: OOMs drop immediately on node-7. Errors down from 120/min to 8/min. Latency starting to recover. :thumbsup:

devops: following up — while disabling continuous batching helps, fragmentation remains on some hosts. Need JVM/PyTorch allocator tuning and longer-term fix. Propose: set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` and enable arena size limits via `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` patch for next deploy. Also consider jemalloc arena tuning for host-level allocators.

nora: agree. short-term hotfix: set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` via a staged daemonset update and restart workers one at a time. That will reduce large-slab allocations that produce arenas.

rahul: I'm drafting a runtime patch: reduce `batching.max_tokens_per_batch` from 4096 -> 1536 for models with long-tail contexts; add a guard to reject >8k token requests for pooled nodes. Also add a metric for per-request kv_cache_bytes to trigger early rejection.

miguel: rolling the envvar on pool-3 now: `kubectl set env ds/kv-runtime PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 -n inference-pool-3` -> scheduled restart. Doing canary on node-7 first.

(5 minutes later)

sara: canary looked good on node-7. memory fragmentation metric trending downward. Starting gradual rollout across pool-3. Keeping batching disabled until we validate.

devops: putting a watch query in Grafana to alert on arena count >10 and kv_cache_bytes > 8GB per GPU. Also added a synthetic test that simulates many long-context requests to detect regression pre-deploy.

anya: customer comms: impacted customers (acct ids) contacted via automated incident email; outreach by AE team for high-priority accounts. No data loss. ETA for full recovery: 40m estimated.

miguel: rollout complete across pool-3. restarting 6 workers, restart spacing 30s. Post-rollout OOMs ~ near zero, throughput at ~95% baseline. Leaving `batching.continuous.enabled=false` until next week when we can test better KV eviction heuristics.

rahul: created PR with allocator changes and batching caps: `github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4521` — includes unit tests and a load validation job. Requesting review from @nora and @devops.

nora: will review. Also recommend we add an automatic fallback policy: if arena_count > 12 then disable continuous batching for that pool automatically.

sara: handoff: I'm sweeping remaining logs and will hand to next oncall (ops-oncall) at 1768005605. Final notes: root cause likely interplay of continuous batching, long-tail context requests, and default CUDA caching allocator behavior that produced arena proliferation and fragmentation -> OOM cascade. Mitigations applied: disable continuous batching (emergency), set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 (hotfix), reduce batch max tokens and add guards (in PR). Customer impact: intermittent 5xxs for ~25 minutes, some throughput loss. No data loss.

ops-oncall: acknowledged — will monitor overnight. please attach postmortem draft and customer timeline. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident incident-1768004321 marked RESOLVED by sara at 1768005605.

sara: filing initial postmortem draft and tagging follow-ups: model runtime changes, allocator tests in CI, and auto-fallback rule.

(END)
